insights.title: Bank credit hits ₹229.9L Cr — fresh high, up ₹6.1L Cr
insights.body: Bank credit outstanding reached ₹229.9L Cr in September 2026, at or near the highest level in this 60-period series. Volume rose ₹6.1L Cr period-on-period (₹223.9L Cr → ₹229.9L Cr).
insights.implication: September's ₹6.1L Cr addition is nearly double August's ₹3.1L Cr gain, keeping the book at a record level for this window.

inferences: Bank credit stood at ₹229.9L Cr in September 2026, up from ₹223.9L Cr in August.
That ₹6.1L Cr addition is close to double the ₹3.1L Cr gain the book made from July (₹220.8L Cr) to August (₹223.9L Cr).
The pickup in monthly additions lines up with the level reaching a fresh high for this 60-period series.

insights.title: Bank credit grew 16.1% in FY26, up 5.1 points from FY25
insights.body: Bank credit grew 11.0% in the year to March 2025 and 16.1% in the year to March 2026. The full-year growth rate stepped up 5.1 points, from 11.0% in FY25 to 16.1% in FY26.
insights.implication: This 5.1-point step-up is unchanged from the last reading, since the figure is fixed at the March close — FY26 remains the clearly faster year of the two, but the reading itself won't move again until the next year-end.

inferences: Bank credit grew 11.0% in FY25 and 16.1% in FY26.
A 5.1-point step-up is a large shift for a once-a-year measure that resets only at each March year-end.
FY26 stands out as the faster lending year of the two on this annual measure.

insights.title: FY26 net new bank credit ₹29.6L Cr — fixed at year-end, near record
insights.body: Banks deployed ₹29.6L Cr of net new credit in the full year to March 2026. This figure is unchanged at ₹29.6L Cr since the March 2026 year-end close, and sits at or near the maximum of this 60-period series.
insights.implication: Because this reading is locked at the March year-end, its steady ₹29.6L Cr value says nothing about conditions since March — the monthly absolute and YoY signals carry that part of the story.

inferences: The FY26 net addition stands at ₹29.6L Cr, unchanged since the March close.
As an annual figure fixed once a year, it does not move with the monthly data between year-ends.
It sits at or near the high end of this 60-period series.

insights.title: Bank credit growth rebounds to 19.38% YoY, a fresh high
insights.body: Bank credit grew 19.38% year-on-year in September 2026, at or near the highest reading in this 36-period series. Growth rose 0.30 points (19.08% → 19.38%), reversing a dip from July's 19.3% to August's 19.1%.
insights.implication: September's rebound to 19.38% erases August's one-month dip and puts growth back at the highest level seen in this 36-period series, well above the 16.2% upper-quartile mark.

inferences: YoY growth climbed to 19.38% in September, up 0.30 points from August's 19.08%.
That rebound reverses August's pullback, when growth had eased from July's 19.3% to 19.1%.
At 19.38%, growth is now at or near the maximum of this 36-period window, well above the 16.2% p75 mark.

insights.title: Food credit falls to ₹0.96L Cr — fourth straight monthly drop
insights.body: Food credit outstanding fell to ₹0.96L Cr in September 2026, down from ₹1.12L Cr in August. Volume declined ₹0.16L Cr period-on-period (₹1.12L Cr → ₹0.96L Cr), the fourth consecutive monthly drop since May's peak of ₹1.37L Cr.
insights.implication: Four consecutive declines from May's ₹1.37L Cr peak have pulled food credit down by ₹0.41L Cr, yet it is still reading in the upper range of this series — the earlier run-up has not been fully unwound.

inferences: Food credit fell to ₹0.96L Cr in September, down from ₹1.12L Cr in August.
This is the fourth straight monthly decline since the ₹1.37L Cr peak in May 2026, a cumulative fall of ₹0.41L Cr.
Despite four months of decline, the level still reads above the p75 mark for this window — the upper range.

insights.title: Food credit YoY cools to 125.71% after August's 145.81% record
insights.body: Food credit grew 125.71% year-on-year in September 2026, down from August's 145.81%. Growth decelerated 20.10 points (145.81% → 125.71%), pulling back from last period's series-high reading.
insights.implication: The 20.10-point pullback from August's record 145.81% is a sharp deceleration, but at 125.71% growth is still far above the 86.8% upper-quartile mark for this series — still one of the strongest readings in the window even after cooling from the peak.

inferences: YoY growth eased to 125.71% in September, down 20.10 points from August's 145.81%.
August's 145.81% had itself been a fresh high, up from July's 107.9%.
Even after this pullback, September's 125.71% remains well above the 86.8% p75 mark for this 48-period window.

insights.title: Non-food credit hits ₹229.0L Cr — fresh high, up ₹6.2L Cr
insights.body: Non-food credit outstanding reached ₹229.0L Cr in September 2026, at or near the highest level in this 60-period series. Volume rose ₹6.2L Cr period-on-period (₹222.8L Cr → ₹229.0L Cr).
insights.implication: September's ₹6.2L Cr addition keeps non-food credit at a fresh high of ₹229.0L Cr, extending a climb that has added ₹96.1L Cr since January 2023.

inferences: Non-food credit rose to ₹229.0L Cr in September, up ₹6.2L Cr from August's ₹222.8L Cr.
That keeps the book at a fresh high for this 60-period series.
Since January 2023's ₹132.9L Cr, the book has added ₹96.1L Cr.

insights.title: Non-food credit FY26 net add ₹29.2L Cr — fixed at year-end
insights.body: Banks deployed ₹29.2L Cr of net new non-food credit in the year to March 2026. This figure is unchanged at ₹29.2L Cr since the March 2026 year-end close, and sits at or near the maximum for this 60-period series.
insights.implication: Because this reading is locked at the March year-end, its steady ₹29.2L Cr value reflects FY26 as a whole rather than any recent shift — the monthly absolute reading is what moves in between.

inferences: The FY26 non-food net addition stands at ₹29.2L Cr, fixed since the March close.
As an annual figure, it won't change again until the next year-end lock in March 2027.
It remains at or near the high end of this 60-period series.

insights.title: Non-food credit growth hits 19.15% YoY — highest in dataset
insights.body: Non-food credit grew 19.15% year-on-year in September 2026. Growth rose from 18.77% in August to 19.15% in September, a 0.38-point pickup that reverses the dip from July's 19.1%.
insights.implication: After one month of easing, non-food credit growth bounced straight back to the highest level in this 36-period series, where the bulk of readings have run between 11.1% and 16.3%.

inferences: Non-food credit grew 19.15% YoY in September 2026, up from 18.77% in August — a 0.38-point increase.
That reverses August's slip from July's 19.1%, when growth had eased for the first time in months.
At 19.15%, this reading is at or near the highest level in this 36-period series, where most history sits between 11.1% and 16.3%.

insights.title: All 4 main sectors positive for a 27th straight period
insights.body: All four main sectors posted positive year-on-year credit growth in September 2026, with the count holding at 4 of 4. Breadth held at 4 of 4 sectors, unchanged from August, extending the all-sectors-positive run to 27 straight periods since July 2024.
insights.implication: Every main sector has now grown together for 27 straight periods, one longer than the 26-period run recorded last month — far outside anything the zero-breadth years before October 2022 showed.

inferences: 4 of 4 main sectors showed positive YoY growth in September 2026, unchanged from August's reading of 4.
This is the 27th consecutive period of 4-of-4 breadth, a run that has held continuously since July 2024.
Across the full 48-period series, breadth sits at or near its maximum, against the stretch through September 2022 when the count read 0.

insights.title: Agriculture's credit share ticks up to 12.31%, still near multi-year lows
insights.body: Agriculture's share of total bank credit was 12.31% in Sep 2026. Share rose 0.08 points from 12.23% in Aug 2026 to 12.31%, staying below the 12.4% level that marks the bottom quarter of this 60-period range.
insights.implication: At 12.31%, agriculture's share has barely moved off last period's 12.23% and stays below the 12.4% level marking the bottom quarter of this 60-period range — a small tick, not a reversal of its slide from 13.0% in Oct 2021.

inferences: Agriculture's share stood at 12.31% in Sep 2026, up 0.08 points from 12.23% in Aug 2026.
A move of that size sits within normal month-to-month noise for a share reading.
At 12.31%, the share is still below the 12.4% mark that defines the bottom quarter of readings across 60 periods.
The share has slid from 13.0% in Oct 2021 to this range, and Sep's tick-up does not reverse that longer slide.

insights.title: Agriculture credit growth climbs to 19.52%, nearing 2024's 20% peak
insights.body: Agriculture credit grew 19.52% YoY in Sep 2026. Growth accelerated 2.30 points from 17.22% in Aug 2026 to 19.52%, moving further above the 17.4% level that marks the top quarter of this range.
insights.implication: Agriculture credit growth has climbed back to 19.52%, within half a point of the 20.0% peak hit in early 2024, after falling as low as 6.8% in Jun 2025 — one of the sharper round-trips in this 48-period series.

inferences: Agriculture credit grew 19.52% YoY in Sep 2026, up 2.30 points from 17.22% in Aug 2026.
That puts growth above the 17.4% mark defining the top quarter of readings across 48 periods.
The series held at 20.0% for three straight months in Jan-Mar 2024 before falling all the way to 6.8% in Jun 2025.
At 19.52%, growth is now within half a point of that 20.0% peak after the sharp slowdown through mid-2025.

insights.title: Industry credit grew 9.1% in FY25, 14.8% in FY26 — a 5.7-point step-up
insights.body: Industry credit's full-year growth stepped up 5.7 points, from 9.1% in the year to Mar 2025 to 14.8% in the year to Mar 2026. Full-year growth rose from 9.1% in FY25 to 14.8% in FY26, a 5.7-point step-up.
insights.implication: Industry credit's annual growth rate jumped 5.7 points between FY25 and FY26, from 9.1% to 14.8% — a step-up fixed at the Mar 2026 year-end, not a trend to read month to month.

inferences: Industry credit grew 9.1% in the year to Mar 2025 and 14.8% in the year to Mar 2026 — a 5.7-point step-up.
This is an annual measure fixed only at each March year-end, not a monthly trajectory.
A 5.7-point jump in full-year growth is a large year-over-year step-up for this sector.

insights.title: Industry's credit share rises to 21.74%, up 0.21 points
insights.body: Industry's share of total bank credit was 21.74% in Sep 2026. Share rose 0.21 points from 21.53% in Aug 2026 to 21.74%.
insights.implication: At 21.74%, industry's share has only just climbed back to the 21.7% mark near the middle of this range, well below the 27.1% it held in Oct 2021 — the broader slide in industry's share of the credit book continues even with this small uptick.

inferences: Industry's share stood at 21.74% in Sep 2026, up 0.21 points from 21.53% in Aug 2026.
That lifts the share back above the 21.7% mark, near the middle of this 60-period range, after touching 21.5% as recently as Aug 2026.
The share has fallen from 27.1% in Oct 2021 to this range, and Sep's uptick is a small move within that longer slide.

insights.title: Industry credit re-accelerates to 19.46% after August's dip
insights.body: Industry credit grew 19.46% YoY in Sep 2026. Growth accelerated 1.23 points from 18.23% in Aug 2026 to 19.46%, nearing the 20.0% peak hit in Jul 2026.
insights.implication: After pulling back to 18.23% in Aug 2026 from Jul's 20.0% peak, industry credit growth has re-accelerated to 19.46% — reading as a brief pause rather than a reversal of the climb from the 5.1% low recorded in Mar 2023.

inferences: Industry credit grew 19.46% YoY in Sep 2026, up 1.23 points from 18.23% in Aug 2026.
That rebound follows Aug's pullback from the 20.0% peak reached in Jul 2026.
At 19.46%, growth sits well above the 13.0% mark that defines the top quarter of readings across 36 periods.

insights.title: Personal Loans is the biggest slice of the parent category at 32.4%
insights.body: Personal Loans holds the largest share of the parent category at 32.4%, Services 28.3%; Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.3%. These are size shares, not growth rates. Top three hold 82.5% of the parent category, spread 20.1 percentage points.
insights.implication: Composition, not momentum: Personal Loans carries the most weight of the parent category. Concentration means the big blocks drive the category — watch them first.

inferences: Personal Loans is the largest block at 32.4% of the parent category.
Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.3% — a 20.1 percentage points spread across 4 sub-categories.
The top three hold 82.5% of the parent category — concentrated mix.

insights.title: Services growing fastest at 28.3%; Personal Loans slowest at 17.3%
insights.body: Services leads YoY growth at 28.3%, Agriculture and Allied Activities at 19.5%; Personal Loans is slowest at 17.3%. 4 of 4 categories growing, spread 11.1 percentage points.
insights.implication: Services is the fastest at 28.3% and the largest block at 28.2% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Services is the standout at 28.3% YoY.
Personal Loans is the weakest at 17.3% — a spread of 11.1 percentage points across 4 categories.
4 of 4 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Personal loans share dips to 32.44%, near mid-range
insights.body: Personal loans held 32.44% of total bank credit in Sep 2026. Share eased from 32.71% last period to 32.44% now, a dip of 0.3 points, sitting within the 30.4%–32.9% range seen over the past 60 periods.
insights.implication: Personal loans' share of total credit has turned down to 32.44% after sitting flat at 32.71% for two periods running — a small reversal rather than an extension of the earlier flat read, still within its 30.4%–32.9% range.

inferences: Personal loans' share fell to 32.44% in Sep 2026, down 0.28 points from 32.71% the prior period.
That keeps it inside the 30.4%–32.9% band seen across the 60-period series, near the middle of that range rather than at an extreme.
The share had held flat at 32.71% for the prior two periods before this dip.

insights.title: Personal loans credit YoY climbs to 17.25%, up 0.33 points
insights.body: Personal loans credit grew 17.25% year-on-year in Sep 2026. Growth rose from 16.92% to 17.25%, a 0.33-point gain, sitting roughly mid-range (12.2%-18.7%) over this 36-period window.
insights.implication: Personal loans growth has climbed steadily since bottoming at 11.1% in May 2025, but at 17.25% it remains well below the 19.1%-21.0% readings seen between Mar and Jun 2023 — this is a recovery, not yet a record.

inferences: Personal loans credit grew 17.25% year-on-year in Sep 2026, up from 16.92% the prior period.
That is a 0.33-point gain, extending a climb that began near 11.1% in May 2025.
At 17.25%, growth now sits roughly in the middle of the 36-period range (12.2% to 18.7%), rather than breaking new ground.

insights.title: Services credit accelerated 10.1 points as FY26 growth hit 20.0%
insights.body: Services credit grew 9.9% in the year to Mar 2025 and 20.0% in the year to Mar 2026. Full-year growth stepped up from 9.9% in FY25 to 20.0% in FY26, a 10.1-point acceleration fixed at the Mar 2026 year-end.
insights.implication: At 10.1 points, this is the sharpest full-year step-up recorded for services credit, with FY26's 20.0% growth more than double FY25's 9.9% pace.

inferences: Services credit grew 9.9% in FY25 and 20.0% in FY26 — a 10.1-point step-up, measured at the Mar 2026 year-end.
Full-year growth moved from single digits to 20.0%, more than doubling between the two year-ends.
This is an annual reading, fixed until the Mar 2027 year-end — it does not move again before then.

insights.title: Services share of credit climbs to 28.34%, near a 60-period high
insights.body: Services accounted for 28.34% of total bank credit in Sep 2026. Share rose from 28.27% to 28.34%, a 0.07-point gain, now at or near the highest level in this 60-period series.
insights.implication: Services' share has not dipped below 28.2% in the months since Mar 2026, and at 28.34% — near the top of this 60-period range — it is extending a steadier climb than the 0.05-point move seen last period.

inferences: Services' share of total bank credit rose to 28.34% in Sep 2026, up 0.07 points from 28.27% in Aug 2026.
That keeps share above the 26.6%-27.7% range covering most of the last 60 periods, and at or near the series maximum.
Share has held at or above 28.2% every month since Mar 2026, when the series first reached that level.

insights.title: Services credit hits 28.32% YoY — highest in this series
insights.body: Services credit grew 28.32% year-on-year in Sep 2026, up from 24.35% in Aug 2026. Growth climbed from 24.35% in Aug 2026 to 28.32% in Sep 2026, a 3.97-point gain, and is now at or near the highest reading in this 36-period series.
insights.implication: At 28.32%, services credit growth is running above the 21.3% level that has historically marked the top of its range, extending an unbroken climb that began at 18.6% in Apr 2026.

inferences: Services credit grew 28.32% year-on-year in Sep 2026, a 3.97-point jump from 24.35% in Aug 2026.
This is the fifth straight monthly rise since the 18.6% dip in Apr 2026, and sits at or near the maximum of a 36-period series whose typical range runs from 11.5% to 21.3%.
Growth is now well above the 21.3% level that has marked the upper quarter of readings in this series.

insights.title: Services took 38.9% of all new bank credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the bank credit added over the past twelve months, Services took 38.9% — the largest share of the new money — growing 28.3% a year and accelerating (+3.97 pp). The rest went to Personal Loans 29.7%; Industry 22.0%; Agriculture and Allied Activities 12.5%. Personal Loans took 29.7% while growing 17.3% a year and accelerating (+0.33 pp) — a smaller slice of a faster-growing total, not a retreat.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's bank credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Services accounts for 38.9% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.

insights.title: Large is the biggest slice of the parent category at 66.5%
insights.body: Large holds the largest share of the parent category at 66.5%, Micro and Small 23.2%; Medium is the smallest at 10.3%. These are size shares, not growth rates. Top three hold 100.0% of the parent category, spread 56.1 percentage points.
insights.implication: Composition, not momentum: Large carries the most weight of the parent category. Concentration means the big blocks drive the category — watch them first.

inferences: Large is the largest block at 66.5% of the parent category.
Medium is the smallest at 10.3% — a 56.1 percentage points spread across 3 sub-categories.
The top three hold 100.0% of the parent category — concentrated mix.

insights.title: Medium growing fastest at 33.2%; Large slowest at 16.0%
insights.body: Medium leads YoY growth at 33.2%, Micro and Small at 24.4%; Large is slowest at 16.0%. 3 of 3 categories growing, spread 17.3 percentage points.
insights.implication: Medium is the fastest at 33.2% and the largest block at 2.2% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Medium is the standout at 33.2% YoY.
Large is the weakest at 16.0% — a spread of 17.3 percentage points across 3 categories.
3 of 3 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Large corporate share of industry credit at a fresh 60-period low
insights.body: Large corporates hold 66.45% of industry credit, at or near the lowest reading in this 60-period series. Share eased further from 66.55% to 66.45%, staying below the 68.7%-73.5% range typical of this series.
insights.implication: At 66.45%, large corporate share sits at or near its lowest point in 60 periods, below even the 68.7% that marks the typical lower bound — the slide, though only 0.10 points this period, keeps the share outside its usual range.

inferences: Large corporate share of industry credit reads 66.45%, at or near the minimum of this 60-period series.
It eased 0.10 points further from 66.55% last period.
The typical range for this series runs from 68.7% to 73.5%, well above where the share now sits.

insights.title: Large corporate credit growth re-accelerates to 15.98% YoY
insights.body: Large corporate credit grew 15.98% YoY, a reading well above the 8.1% upper end of this series' typical range. Growth re-accelerated from 14.88% to 15.98% this period, reversing last period's slowdown from 17.69% to 14.88%.
insights.implication: Growth re-accelerating to 15.98% after dipping to 14.88% shows last period's slowdown from 17.69% did not continue — large corporate credit growth is picking back up, not settling into a cooling trend.

inferences: Large corporate credit grew 15.98% YoY this period, up 1.10 points from 14.88% last period.
That 14.88% reading had itself been a slowdown from 17.69% the period before, so this period's move reverses that deceleration.
At 15.98%, growth sits well above the 8.1% upper end of this series' typical range (48 periods).

insights.title: Medium enterprises' industry-credit share hits 10.33%, a fresh high
insights.body: Medium enterprises held 10.33% of industry credit in Sep 2026, up from 10.19% the prior period. Share rose from 10.19% to 10.33%, continuing the climb from 10.0% → 10.2% → 10.3% over the last three periods.
insights.implication: Medium enterprises have added to their industry-credit share for a third straight period, pushing past the 9.2% upper-range mark to a fresh high of 10.33%.

inferences: Medium enterprises' share of industry credit rose to 10.33% in Sep 2026, up 0.14pp from 10.19% in Aug 2026.
This is at or near the highest reading in this 60-period series, well above the 9.2% mark that bounds its upper range.
The share has now risen for three straight periods, from 9.9% in Jun 2026 to 10.33% in Sep 2026.

insights.title: Medium enterprise credit growth accelerates to 33.24% YoY
insights.body: Medium enterprise credit grew 33.24% YoY in Sep 2026, up from 31.78% the prior period. Growth rose from 31.78% to 33.24%, up 1.46pp, extending a climb that has run from 30.3% in Jun 2026 to 33.24% now.
insights.implication: Medium enterprise growth has now held above 30% for four straight periods and is still climbing, reaching 33.24% against a 20.4% mark that typically bounds this line's upper range.

inferences: Medium enterprise credit grew 33.24% YoY in Sep 2026, up 1.46pp from 31.78% in Aug 2026.
This is at or near the highest reading in this 48-period series, well clear of the 20.4% mark that bounds its upper range.
Growth has now held above 30% for four consecutive periods: 30.3% in Jun, 30.5% in Jul, 31.8% in Aug, 33.2% in Sep.

insights.title: Micro & Small credit accelerates 23.2 points, FY25 to FY26
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprise credit grew 9.4% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 32.7% in the year ending Mar 2026, a 23.2 percentage point acceleration. Full-year growth stepped up from 9.4% in FY25 to 32.7% in FY26, a 23.2-point move. This is an annual figure set at the March year-end; it does not change month to month.
insights.implication: The 23.2-point step-up between FY25's 9.4% and FY26's 32.7% shows Micro & Small credit's annual growth pace shifting sharply higher within a single year.

inferences: Micro & Small credit grew 9.4% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 32.7% in the year ending Mar 2026.
The gap between these two full-year rates is 23.2 percentage points, an annual step-up rather than a monthly move.
A move of this size marks a sharp shift in the yearly pace of Micro & Small lending between FY25 and FY26.

insights.title: Micro & Small share steady at 23.22%, just off its high
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprises held 23.22% of industry credit in Sep 2026, down slightly from 23.26% the prior period. Share held nearly flat, easing from 23.26% to 23.22%, staying within the series' highest band of 23.1%–23.5% seen since Jan 2026.
insights.implication: At 23.22%, Micro & Small's share is essentially unchanged from 23.26% and still sits in the series' upper range, just below the 23.5% high reached in Jan 2026.

inferences: Micro & Small's share stood at 23.22% in Sep 2026, down 0.04pp from 23.26% in Aug 2026.
A move of 0.04pp is within the ±0.5pp band treated as noise for a share signal, so this is not a structural shift.
The share remains above the 22.2% mark that bounds the upper range of this series, close to the January 2026 high of 23.5%.

insights.title: Micro & Small credit growth rises to 24.42% YoY
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprise credit grew 24.42% YoY in Sep 2026, up from 22.96% the prior period. Growth rose from 22.96% to 24.42%, up 1.46pp, a second straight increase after easing from the 32.7% peak in Mar 2026.
insights.implication: Growth has now risen for two consecutive periods, to 24.42%, after easing from the Mar 2026 peak of 32.7%, though it remains below that high.

inferences: Micro & Small credit grew 24.42% YoY in Sep 2026, up 1.46pp from 22.96% in Aug 2026.
This sits above the 22.5% mark that bounds the upper range of this 48-period series, though still below the 32.7% peak reached in Mar 2026.
The increase extends the rebound that began last period, when growth rose to 22.96% after easing from the Mar 2026 peak.

insights.title: MSME-large corporate growth spread widens to 8.4 points
insights.body: MSME credit grew 8.4 percentage points faster than large corporate credit in Sep 2026, up from 8.1pp the prior period. The spread widened slightly from 8.1pp to 8.4pp, building on the move off the Jul 2026 low of 4.9pp.
insights.implication: The spread has now widened for two straight periods since its 4.9pp low in Jul 2026, reaching 8.4pp, though it sits roughly in the middle of this series' range rather than at an extreme.

inferences: The MSME-vs-large-corporate growth spread stood at 8.4pp in Sep 2026, up 0.4pp from 8.1pp in Aug 2026.
This follows the Jul 2026 low of 4.9pp, after which the spread widened to 8.1pp and now to 8.4pp.
A widening spread means MSME credit is pulling further ahead of large corporate credit in year-on-year growth terms.

insights.title: Large took 56.2% of all new industry credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the industry credit added over the past twelve months, Large took 56.2% — the largest share of the new money — growing 16.0% a year and accelerating (+1.10 pp). The rest went to Micro and Small 28.0%; Medium 15.8%.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's industry credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Large accounts for 56.2% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.

insights.title: Housing Finance Companies holds 17.3% of NBFC credit; Public Financial Institutions 16.4%
insights.body: RBI breaks NBFC credit into two sub-categories. Housing Finance Companies holds 17.3% and Public Financial Institutions 16.4% — these are size shares, not growth rates. Together the two break-outs cover 33.6% of NBFC credit; the rest is not sub-classified in the RBI statement.
